title: Illustrative Games: Chapters 1–3
subtitle: Master Case Studies in Development, Files, and Ranks
summary: Full annotated master game: Nimzowitsch vs. Alapin (Vilnius 1912) illustrating the deadly penalty of early queen pawn-hunting against rapid central development and open-file invasion.
aphorism: Theory without living practice is a sterile tree. Let the master games demonstrate our principles in battle.
attribution: 100th Anniversary Centenary Edition. Based directly on Aron Nimzowitsch's My System (1925), Part I, Chapter 3a, Game 1.

body.historicalContext: In this famous miniature from Vilnius 1912, Nimzowitsch punished Semion Alapin for greedily hunting pawns with his queen while neglecting development, culminating in a legendary double-rook sacrifice and queen sacrifice on d8.

sections.title: The Fruits of Development and Open Files
sections.markdown:
We have analyzed the **center**, **democratic development**, **open files**, and the **seventh and eighth ranks**.

Now we witness these elements synthesized in **Nimzowitsch vs. Alapin (Vilnius 1912)**. When Black goes pawn-hunting with **9...Qxg2?**, Nimzowitsch uses the open e- and d-files to unleash a stunning tactical assault.

engineLens.takeaway: Stockfish confirms that Nimzowitsch's piece sacrifices 12.O-O-O!, 14.Bf6!!, and 17.Qd8+! force mate in all lines.
